questions.q: Explain Rawls' idea of the 'veil of ignorance' as a way of thinking about justice.

answer.text: When people decide the rules of society, they usually favour arrangements that benefit their own position. A rich person may support low taxes and a poor person high welfare. This self-interest makes it hard to agree on what is truly just.

To overcome this, the philosopher John Rawls suggested that we imagine ourselves behind a veil of ignorance. Behind this veil, a person does not know what position they will occupy in society, whether they will be rich or poor, upper or lower caste, able-bodied or disabled, talented or not.

Not knowing their own future place, rational people would choose rules that are fair to everyone, and especially would protect the interests of the worst-off, since they themselves might end up in that position.

answer: In this way the veil of ignorance provides an impartial method for arriving at principles of justice as fairness.

questions.q: What are the main dimensions of justice, and how are they related?

answer.text: means giving each person their due, and it has several dimensions that together make a society just.

list: Social justice means equal treatment and no discrimination on grounds of caste, race, sex or religion
Economic justice means a fair distribution of wealth and opportunity so that no one is left in want
Political justice means equal political rights and a share in power for all

answer.text: One is incomplete without the others.

list: Political equality means little without a decent standard of living
So true justice requires social, economic and political fairness together

questions.q: How does Rawls argue that a just distribution of resources should benefit the least advantaged?

answer.text: argued that a fair society is one whose rules we would choose from behind a 'veil of ignorance', not knowing our own place in it.

list: Not knowing whether we would be rich or poor, able or disabled, we would want rules that protect the worst-off
We would not gamble on being at the bottom of an unequal society

answer.lead: This leads to a key principle.
answer.text: Inequalities are just only if they help the least advantaged.

list: Some inequality may be allowed if it improves the position of the poorest, for example by rewarding effort that benefits all
So a just distribution must give special weight to the needs of the least advantaged
